conformator_home_intro: Conformator tests whether banks, payment service providers and third-party providers implement the open banking APIs, security profile and consent rules correctly. Tests run against participants' non-production systems. The regulator reviews the results and issues conformance reports.
conformator_home_not_a_licence: A conformance report shows that a system passed the technical tests it lists. It is not a licence, and it does not give access to live data or payments.
conformator_home_who_participants: {#strong}Participants{/strong}: banks, payment service providers, fintechs and third-party providers. They add their non-production systems, run tests, give evidence and submit their results.
conformator_home_who_staff: {#strong}The regulator's staff{/strong}: they keep the test catalogue, admit participants, review submissions and issue reports. Reviewers assess the tests a person must decide; approvers make the final decision. Nobody does both for the same submission.
conformator_home_who_anyone: {#strong}Anyone{/strong} can read the test catalogue and check a report.
conformator_home_catalogue_rules: The regulator's rules are recorded as {#strong}requirements{/strong}, one per clause. Tests are grouped into {#strong}suites{/strong}, each for one kind of system (an API provider such as a bank, an authorisation server, or an API consumer such as a third-party provider) and one family of APIs (account information, payment initiation, funds confirmation, consent or security). Each {#strong}test{/strong} has an ID that never changes, names the requirements it covers, says what a pass looks like, and is mandatory or not.
conformator_home_catalogue_versions: A suite is a draft until it is approved. An approved suite never changes: a change is a new version, so every result keeps its meaning.
conformator_home_kinds: There are three kinds of test:
conformator_home_kind_automated: {#strong}Automated{/strong}: the runner calls the participant's system and checks the answers.
conformator_home_kind_evidence: {#strong}Evidence review{/strong}: the participant gives evidence, such as a policy or an audit record, and a reviewer decides.
conformator_home_kind_control: {#strong}Organisational control{/strong}: a reviewer decides whether the organisation has something in place, such as a named person responsible for security.
conformator_home_run_runner: A participant starts a run of an approved suite against one of their systems. The {#strong}runner{/strong}, a separate service, carries out each automated test's steps in order, as a real caller of the system would: over mutual TLS with its own certificate, as its own client of the system or on behalf of a test customer. A step sends a request, checks the answer (its status, fields, headers, or its shape against the suite's OpenAPI document), and can keep a value, such as a consent's id, for later steps. Security checks of an authorisation server are handed to the OpenID Foundation's conformance suite.
conformator_home_outcomes: Each test in a run gets one outcome:
conformator_home_outcome_pass: {#strong}pass{/strong}: every step did what the test expects;
conformator_home_outcome_fail: {#strong}fail{/strong}: the system answered, but not as expected, and the result says how;
conformator_home_outcome_blocked: {#strong}blocked{/strong}: the test could not go on. The result says whose side stopped it: the participant's (their system could not be reached) or the test platform's (the runner lacked something). A test platform problem is never counted against the participant;
conformator_home_outcome_not_executed: {#strong}not executed{/strong}: an evidence or control test, waiting for a reviewer;
conformator_home_run_kept: Every result keeps the requests and responses, with tokens and secrets hidden, and their correlation ids.
conformator_home_report_title: From a run to a report
conformator_home_report_submit: The participant {#strong}submits{/strong} a finished run for review, and gives evidence for the evidence and control tests.
conformator_home_report_review: A {#strong}reviewer{/strong} assesses those tests. An automated result cannot be overridden, unless the participant appeals it and the appeal is upheld.
conformator_home_report_waiver: The participant can ask for a {#strong}waiver{/strong} of a test. An approved waiver has an end date, never changes the test's outcome, and is shown wherever the outcome is.
conformator_home_report_approve: An {#strong}approver{/strong}, who did not assess the submission, makes the final decision. A submission can be approved only when every mandatory test passed, is not applicable, or has an approved waiver.
conformator_home_report_issue: Approval issues a {#strong}conformance report{/strong}, digitally signed, with a reference such as CR-2026-7K3QX9MD. Anyone can check it on this site, or check its signature without this site using the published key. A report expires, and can be superseded by a newer one or withdrawn.
conformator_home_data: Everything is kept in OBP-API, as dynamic entities. The catalogue, the participant register and the reports are in one central space. Each participant's systems, runs, results, evidence and the regulator's decisions about them are in a space of their own, so OBP-API's Roles keep each participant's data apart from every other's. Secrets the runner needs, such as client certificates, are kept by the runner, never in OBP-API.
conformator_prepare_intro: Conformator tests open banking systems against the regulator's rules, and turns the results into signed conformance reports. These are the steps, in order.
conformator_prepare_progress_shown: Each step shows how far you have got.
conformator_prepare_log_in_for_progress: Log in to see how far you have got.
conformator_prepare_intro_admin: Done once, by an OBP-API administrator, before anyone else can use Conformator. The {#setup}setup page{/setup} shows every piece in detail.
conformator_prepare_intro_regulator: For the regulator's staff, who keep the catalogue, admit participants, review their results and issue reports.
conformator_prepare_intro_participant: For banks, payment service providers and third-party providers testing their systems.
conformator_prepare_how_parts_fit: How the parts fit together, from requirements to reports, is on the {#home}home page{/home}.
conformator_step_see_on_setup: See it on the setup page
conformator_step_who_admin_manager: An administrator, in the API Manager.
conformator_step_space_what: The central space is a bank in OBP-API, with the bank_id {space}. It holds the test catalogue, the participant register and the issued reports. Staff Roles are granted there, so they reach nothing else in OBP-API.
conformator_step_space_action: Create it in the API Manager
conformator_step_space_missing: The bank {space} does not exist yet.
conformator_step_app_what: Mark Conformator’s Consumer as a Platform App in the API Manager and grant it the Scopes it asks for. With them, it creates the definitions of the records it keeps in the central space.
conformator_step_app_missing: It is missing some Scopes; the setup page lists them.
conformator_step_app_ready: It holds every Scope, and its records are ready.
conformator_step_app_not_ready: It holds every Scope; its records are not all ready yet.
conformator_step_runner_what: The runner is the separate service that calls participants’ systems. Start it, put its consumer_id in Conformator’s settings (CONFORMATOR_RUNNER_CONSUMER_ID), then mark it as a Platform App and grant it its Scope in the central space.
conformator_step_runner_who: An administrator: the settings on the server, the Scopes in the API Manager.
conformator_step_runner_action: Open the runner in Platform Apps
conformator_step_runner_set: Its consumer_id is set. Check its Scope in Platform Apps.
conformator_step_runner_unset: Its consumer_id is not set yet.
conformator_step_signing_what: Conformator signs every conformance report, so anyone can check it. Make an Ed25519 key, keep it out of the repository, and point REPORT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE at it.
conformator_step_signing_action: See how on the setup page
conformator_step_staff_title: Give the regulator’s staff their Roles
conformator_step_staff_what: Staff ask for the Roles they need on the setup page. Accept their requests in the API Manager, or grant Roles there directly. Give reviewing and approving to different people.
conformator_step_staff_action_setup: See the Roles on the setup page
conformator_step_staff_none_waiting: No staff Role request is waiting.
conformator_step_roles_what: Staff Roles let you keep the catalogue, register participants and issue reports. Ask for the ones you need on the setup page; an administrator accepts them in the API Manager.
conformator_step_catalogue_what: Record your rules as requirements, then make a suite of tests for one kind of system and one family of APIs. Choose an OBP API version or an OpenAPI file, and Conformator suggests the tests’ IDs and titles.
conformator_step_approve_what: A suite is a draft until it is approved. Participants can run only approved suites, and an approved suite never changes: a change is a new version.
conformator_step_participant_what: Register the bank, payment service provider or third-party provider, naming the first admin of its Organisation, then admit it and set up its own space. The Organisation’s members get access to the space, so they can log in and test.
conformator_step_review_what: When a participant submits a run, a reviewer assesses the tests a person must decide, and an approver who did not assess it makes the final decision. Approval issues a signed conformance report.
conformator_step_review_who: Reviewers and approvers. Nobody does both for the same submission.
conformator_step_review_none: No report has been issued yet.
conformator_step_login_what: Log in with the account your organisation uses for the regulator’s sandbox.
conformator_step_join_what: The regulator registers your organisation and adds you to its space, where your systems, runs and results are kept apart from everyone else’s. If you cannot see it, ask the regulator to add you.
conformator_step_join_none: You do not belong to a space yet.
conformator_step_system_what: Add your non-production system: what it is (an API provider, an authorisation server or an API consumer), its address, and the client id your sandbox gave the runner. Secrets are never kept here.
conformator_step_run_what: Choose an approved suite and start a run against your system. The runner calls your system as a real partner would, and records each request, response and outcome: pass, fail or blocked.
conformator_step_submit_what: Fix what failed and run again. When you are ready, submit a finished run for review, with evidence for the tests a person must decide. You can ask for a waiver of a test, or appeal a result.
conformator_step_report_what: When the regulator approves your submission, Conformator issues a signed conformance report. Anyone can check it by its reference, such as CR-2026-7K3QX9MD.
conformator_step_report_who: The regulator approves; anyone can check the report.
conformator_catalogue_unreadable: The catalogue could not be read: {error}
conformator_suite_openapi: Responses are checked against {#openapi}this OpenAPI document{/openapi}.
conformator_tests_none: This suite has no tests yet.
conformator_tests_how_runner: A participant starts a run of this suite against one of their non-production systems. The runner then carries out each automated test's steps in order, calling the system's APIs the way a third-party provider would: over mutual TLS with its own certificate, as its own client of the system or on behalf of a test customer. A value kept from one answer (such as a consent's id) is used in later steps. The test passes when every answer is as expected; the result says exactly which expectation was not met.
conformator_tests_how_people: Evidence and control tests are not run by the runner. The participant gives evidence, and one of the regulator's reviewers decides.
conformator_tests_no_steps: This test has no steps yet.
conformator_tests_steps_broken: Its steps have problems, so it cannot run yet.
conformator_tests_person_decides: A person decides this test. The participant gives: {evidence}. A reviewer then assesses it as passed, failed or not applicable.
conformator_tests_default_evidence: the evidence the regulator asks for
conformator_reports_intro: Give the reference printed on the report, such as CR-2026-7K3QX9MD. You will see whether it is genuine, unchanged and still valid.
conformator_reports_public_key_link: The public key reports are signed with
conformator_report_bad_hash: its content does not match its hash
conformator_report_unknown_key: it was not signed with the published key
conformator_report_print: Print this page to keep a PDF.
conformator_report_withdraw_log_in: Log in to withdraw a report.
conformator_report_withdraw_reason: Give the reason for withdrawing it.
conformator_report_withdraw_only_valid: Only a valid report can be withdrawn.
conformator_report_withdrawn_done: The report is withdrawn. Anyone checking it now sees that, with your reason.
